Congrats to the Thinking Machines Lab team on the release of Inkling! Inkling is a fully open-weight (Apache 2.0) 975B-A41B MoE model with native support for text, image, and audio inputs, featuring a context window of up to 1M tokens. It leads all U.S. open-weight models on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. We’ve tested it internally and seen strong performance across reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks. Inkling has day-one support on Tinker, and we're excited to start running experiments with it. AfterQuery is proud to have supplied data that helped train the model. ...more ...more

Today, we’re announcing Naïve has raised a $28.5 million Series A to build autonomous company infrastructure. This round was led by Nexus, with participation from Y Combinator, Zetta, Liquid 2, and more. Dennis Zax & I have been building together since we were 14. We sold our first company as teenagers, dropped out of Berkeley, joined Y Combinator, and spent the last several years thinking about what the world looks like when agents can fully run businesses. Coding agents can now ship an app in an afternoon. But turning that app into a real operating business still takes months. Developers manually stitch together payments, incorporation, email, phone numbers, compute, memory, databases, authentication, and dozens of other services — infra built for human operators, not autonomous agents. Naïve is rebuilding and unifying the entire business stack for agents. Today, thousands of developers write a single config file, and Naïve provisions everything their agents need behind one API: > Real-world Identity: KYC/KYB, LLC formation, Email, Phone, Virtual Cards > Cloud: Database, Hosting, Compute, Storage, Auth > Serverless Agents: Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, Vetta > Orchestration: Task Management, Interagent Communication, Scheduling > Inference / Model Routing > Memory: One context layer that grows with the entire company. > 10k+ Tool Gateway: Stripe, Github, Quickbooks, Higgsfield, Browser, etc. > Governance: Enforce capability policies, audit logs, HITL approval With this new capital, we’re investing deeply into our new lab with four research areas: serverless agents, inference, brain, and agent workforce orchestration. Our early benchmarks can start an agent in 2.3 milliseconds using 1.2MB, reduce inference costs several-fold, and achieve stronger memory recall with 11x fewer tokens per query. In this next decade, agent spend is set to scale into the trillions as companies completely run on agents that finish work autonomously. Our vision with our research is to make each token do more, so autonomous companies can become a cost-efficient reality. Thank you to all our investors including: Abhishek Sharma (Partner @ Nexus) Andrew Miklas , Diana Hu (Partners @ YC) Apoorva Pandhi (GP @ Zetta VP) Raj Singh (GP @ Z21 Ventures) Jimmy Cho (Investor, DEEPCORE (Softbank)) Michael Ma (Partner, Liquid 2 Ventures) Vijay Krishnan (Co-Founder of Turing) Gokul Rajaram JD Sherman (Former Hubspot President) Allison Pickens (Former Gainsight COO) Tim Zheng (Founder of Apollo) Robert Chatwani (President @ Docusign) Zach Sims (Founder of Codeacademy) Gert Lanckriet (Head of ML @ Amazon) Eric Ciarla (Co-Founder of Firecrawl) We’re now hiring benchmark-breakers who want to push the frontier of agent business infrastructure. Some conferences change what you know. Others change what you believe is possible. AMD Advancing AI 2026 was both. As a 19-year-old podcaster and entrepreneur, receiving a press pass to cover one of the biggest AI conferences in the world at Moscone Center definitely wasn't on my bingo card. 😉 Even more special, I got to experience it alongside my dad. 😊 Over two incredible days, I met founders, students, researchers, engineers, investors, journalists, creators, and leaders from companies including AMD, HPE, Supermicro, IBM, Nutanix, Cisco, Synopsys, Arista, AWS, Dell, Microsoft, and many more. I also had the chance to hear remarkable conversations from leaders at OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Hugging Face, Cisco, AT&T, and other organizations as they joined Lisa Su and the AMD team on stage during the keynote to discuss where AI is headed. One of the coolest parts of the conference? Seeing robots, physical AI, and technologies that felt like they were straight out of science fiction. 🤖🦾🦿 But the moment I'll remember forever happened because of one simple idea. "O'ChakDe" (the name of my podcast) means "Go For It." So... I did. I cold-approached AMD Chair and CEO Dr. Lisa Su, introduced myself, asked if she'd be willing to do a quick interview, and somehow... she said yes. Thirty seconds. One conversation. A memory I'll carry for the rest of my life. I shared the interview on July 24, and to my surprise, it quickly went viral across Instagram and LinkedIn. In just over a week, with the momentum still growing every day, the clip has already reached: 📈 700,000+ Instagram views 📈 500,000+ Instagram accounts reached 📈 234,000+ LinkedIn impressions & 1.1K+ likes ...and it's still climbing. 🙏 It was surreal, but what means even more to me than the numbers are the messages and comments from students, founders, and young creators saying the video inspired them to ask, reach out, and take their shot. That means everything. One of my favorite parts of the conference was seeing so many familiar faces from The O'ChakDe Show. Over the past few years, I've had the privilege of interviewing founders, Fortune 500 executives, investors, and innovators in person, and it was amazing to reconnect with many of them at AMD Advancing AI 2026 while also meeting so many new people. I'm incredibly grateful to AMD for hosting such an inspiring event and to everyone who took a few minutes to chat, take a selfie, share advice, or simply say hello. Every conversation taught me something. Sometimes all it takes is one conversation, one question, or one moment of courage. Go for it. That's what O'ChakDe has always meant. And after this week, I believe it more than ever. ❤️🚀 #AMD #AdvancingAI #SiliconValley #PhysicalAI #LisaSu
